n: Another message arrives. Chapter 7 is a poem of alarm, with short, hammering phrases like a warning bell.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me

n: “An end! The end has come” on the whole land of Israel, in every direction. Amos had used the same stark word about the northern kingdom.

f.w: An end, the end is come
the four corners of the land
f.g: The whole land, from every direction.

n: God will judge Judah by its own ways and repay it for its detestable practices. Consequences match choices.
Judah’s own sins will be in its midst, visible to all. Through the consequences they will finally recognize the Lord.

f.w: mine eye shall not spare thee

n: A unique, unprecedented disaster is arriving.

f.g: A one-of-a-kind calamity; some manuscripts read “disaster after disaster.”

n: The end is personified as an enemy who has been “watching”—lying in wait—and now arrives. In Hebrew, “end” (qets) and “awake/watch” (heqits) make a wordplay.
Doom (or “the morning”) has come; the day of trouble is near—not the joyful shouting of harvest festivals on the mountains.

f.g: The Hebrew word is uncertain; possibly “doom” or “your turn.”

f.w: the sounding again of the mountains
f.g: Probably joyful shouts, as at harvest or festival time.

n: God will soon pour out his fury and judge according to their ways—echoing verse 3.
A new title appears: “the LORD that smiteth.” Israel will recognize God as the one who strikes when they refuse correction.

“The rod has blossomed, pride has budded”: wickedness has come to full flower and is ready to bear fruit—or the “rod” of punishment (Babylon) is ready. Compare Aaron’s budding rod, which once confirmed God’s chosen priesthood.
Violence has grown into a rod that will punish wickedness. Nothing of their wealth or crowds will remain, and the destruction will be so complete there will be no one left to mourn.

f.w: neither shall there be wailing for them

n: Normal business means nothing now. Buyers shouldn’t celebrate their bargain, nor sellers mourn their loss, because all property is about to be lost anyway.

f.w: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn

n: Land sold under the law would usually return to its family in the Jubilee year—but not this time. Exile will undo all transactions.

f.w: the seller shall not return to that which is sold
f.g: Under the Jubilee law, sold family land was restored every fiftieth year.

n: The trumpet sounds a call to arms, but no one goes out to fight—courage is gone because God’s wrath is upon them.
The sword outside the city and famine and plague inside—there is no safe place.
Survivors will hide in the mountains, moaning like doves, each mourning for his own sins.

f.g: Doves’ cooing was compared to mourning.

n: Terror will drain their strength: hands go limp, and knees turn to water.

f.w: all knees shall be weak as water
f.g: Possibly a vivid idiom for losing bladder control from fear.

n: They will wear sackcloth and shave their heads in mourning, covered with horror and shame.

f.g: Shaving the head was a sign of mourning.

n: People will throw their silver and gold into the streets as worthless. Wealth, which had become their stumbling block and even the material of their idols, cannot save them in the day of the Lord.

f.w: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them

n: God gave them beautiful jewelry, but they used it to make idols. So he will take it away from them.

f.g: Their gold and silver jewelry—or possibly the temple, Israel’s glorious ornament.

f.w: they made the images of their abominations

n: Their treasures will go to foreigners as plunder, who will profane them.
God will turn his face away, allowing robbers to enter and defile his “secret place”—the temple’s Holy of Holies.

f.g: His treasured place—the temple and its inner sanctuary.

f.w: My face will I turn also from them

n: Prepare a chain for captives, because the land is full of bloodshed and violence.

f.g: Prepare chains for prisoners being led into exile.

n: God will bring the most ruthless of nations to take their homes. Their proud strength will end, and their sanctuaries will be defiled.
Terror comes; they will look for peace but find none—the false prophets’ promises of “peace” will fail.

f.w: they shall seek peace, and there shall be none

n: Disaster on disaster, rumor on rumor. Desperate people will seek a vision from a prophet, instruction from a priest, or advice from elders—but none will have answers.

f.w: the law shall perish from the priest

n: King, prince, and commoner alike will despair. God will judge them by their own standards, and they will know he is the LORD.
